mechanisms.decisive_claim: For some L(N)->infinity with L(N)=o(log N), the minimal unbalanced relation hypergraph induced on (N^(1-1/L),N] has an o(N)-vertex transversal, uniformly in N; deleting the lower tail and this transversal gives the finite density-one theorem.
mechanisms.kill_test: Use prime-labelled unequal-shore incidence circuits to seek a positive-density family of almost disjoint minimal supports forcing a linear transversal.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every bad relation inside the high tail contains a bad subrelation whose larger shore has at most L(N) elements.
mechanisms.kill_test: Construct a minimal K_(s+1,s) edge-prime relation with s>L(N) and place it wholly above N^(1-1/L).

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Restricting to squarefree integers makes every minimal exponent relation balanced, so deleting nonsquarefree integers suffices.
mechanisms.kill_test: The K_(s+1,s) edge-prime construction is squarefree on every vertex and has shore imbalance one.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every finite distinct-factor admissible set admits a rational totally additive function taking value one on all admitted integers.
mechanisms.kill_test: Test the exact admissible set {2,4} against 2v(2)-v(4)=0.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: For one growing finite selected-prime set P, the exact-one cylinder {n:sum_(p in P)nu_p(n)=1} retains the additive level-one certificate and its natural density can tend to one.
mechanisms.kill_test: Compute the cylinder density as product(1-1/p) sum(1/p) and optimize it over lambda=sum 1/p.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: A common linear dilation distinctifies any repeated unbalanced relation while preserving its product equality, so the repetitions-allowed obstruction transfers to the active variant.
mechanisms.kill_test: Track the common dilation parameter on the r- and s-factor shores and compare its homogeneous degrees.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Natural density 1-o(1) forces all entries of a fixed nonlinear polarization pattern such as (2x)(2y)=4xy, uniformly at the scale needed for a distinct unbalanced relation.
mechanisms.kill_test: Use the finite high tail (N^(2/3),N], which has density one and deletes every possible output 4xy<=N together with its small inputs.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: All but o(N) integers in [N] can be assigned pairwise distinct prime divisors, and private-prime cancellation then proves admissibility.
mechanisms.kill_test: Compare the required matching size (1-o(1))N with the pi(N) available prime vertices.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: After removing an o(N) smooth core, charge each minimal unbalanced circuit to a largest-prime fibre and select exposed endpoints with total cost at most O(log log N) times the explicit logarithmic fractional cover; this gives O(N log log N/log N)=o(N) deletions.
mechanisms.kill_test: Compute exposure and congestion on K_(s+1,s), complete unequal-shore graphs, and circuits in which every large-prime fibre has degree two.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: A fixed prime-exponent dimension alone bounds every distinct-factor admissible family by an absolute constant, independent of exponent height.
mechanisms.kill_test: Use powers 2^(2^j), whose one-dimensional exponent vectors have unique subset sums for arbitrarily many j.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The minimal-relation ILP on the high tail has an explicit fractional cover of weight o(N) and a rank-sensitive rounding theorem with o(N) additive loss, uniformly over the unbounded circuit sizes.
mechanisms.kill_test: Search exact small-N duals and prime-incidence circuit families for a linear integrality gap or unavoidable positive fractional mass.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The union of independently admissible numerical blocks remains admissible, so finite near-optima can be concatenated directly into a natural-density set.
mechanisms.kill_test: Take admissible blocks {2,3} and {6}; their union contains 2*3=6.
